issues.description: Behavioral change: s.state[k] = sorted now only runs when yield returns true, altering early-termination semantics.
issues.detail: Previously the sorted marker was set unconditionally after pop; now it only fires on yield(node)==true. Correctness now depends on the deferred clear wiping state when the caller bails early. Probably fine, but it's an undocumented state-machine change in a PR sold as cleanup. Add a comment tying early-return correctness to the defer.

issues.description: Collapsing working/walking and moving cleanup into defer changes the Sorter contract without stated invariants or precondition.
issues.detail: The two labels previously encoded distinct DFS phases that push() reads; merging them is a real data-model change, not a rename. Cleanup moving from entry to defer also shifts the lifetime contract for reuse. Either is fine if correct, but the diff ships without a stated loop invariant, termination argument, or precondition on Sort() entry. Write the invariant.

issues.description: Three independent changes squashed into one diff: state collapse, stack-reset fix, yield-ordering change.
issues.detail: The patch bundles (1) working/walking collapse, (2) s.stack[0:] no-op replaced with clear()+[:0], and (3) moving s.state[k]=sorted inside the yield branch. Each has separate reasoning and risk. Squashing defeats bisect and obscures review. Split into three commits with distinct messages.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR title is 'Fix state reuse' but no test calling Sort() twice on the same Sorter is added. Without it, the next refactor silently reintroduces the bug, and the correctness claim rests on assertion rather than proof. Add a Sort()-twice regression test.

issues.description: Comment typos in the load-bearing algorithm explanation: 'visisted' and 'if its'.
issues.detail: The rewritten comment reads 'whether this node has been visisted and if its the first or second visit'. Fix to 'visited' and 'it's'. This comment is the only prose explaining why each node is visited twice; spelling matters here.

issues.description: clear(s.stack) before reslicing to zero length needs a one-line justification.
issues.detail: If the stack holds pointer-bearing entries, clear() is right for GC; if values, it's ceremony. Either way, the original s.stack[0:] was a no-op bug and the new clear()+[:0] is correct, but state intent in a comment so a future reader doesn't 'optimize' it away.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK but close. The panel agrees the underlying fixes are real: s.stack[0:] was a no-op, the working/walking duplication was gratuitous, and the sorted-marker placement needed attention. But the diff bundles three independent changes, ships without a stated loop invariant or precondition for Sorter reuse, silently changes the early-return postcondition, and lacks a regression test for the very bug it claims to fix. Split the patch, add a Sort()-twice test, state the invariant, and fix the comment typos before landing.
